 BEMT 101: What Every Dermatologist Should Know About the Newly Approved Sunscreen Filter
 By Zoe Diana Draelos, MD 
 Recently, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the first new sunscreen filter in more than 20 years! Many sunscreen makers have been or are in the process of rolling out their BEMT formulations.
 What is it?
 Bemotrizinol, abbreviated as BEMT, is also known as Tinosorb S globally with the US trade name of Parsol Shield. BEMT is an organic filter, meaning it is broken down with ultraviolet (UV) exposure, undergoing a chemical reaction as part of the protective process, but it is more photostable than other traditional organic filters. The US government has approved its use in concentrations of up to 6% and has given it Generally Recognized as Safe and Effective (GRASE) ingredient status, so it can be used by children aged six months and older along with adults.
 BEMT is chemically known as Bis-Ethylhexyloxyphenol Methoxyphenyl Triazine. The triazine core, coupled with the conjugated aromatic system, allows conversion of UV energy to heat energy without quick product breakdown. It is a broad-spectrum filter, meaning it can provide protection against both UVA and UVB radiation.
 BEMT provides photoprotection between 310nm and 400nm, covering both the UVB and UVA spectrum. The 310nm photoprotection in the UVB range protects against sunburn and direct DNA damage, while 340–345nm protects against skin aging and deeper penetration of the UV radiation.
 What does this mean for dermatologists and their patients?
 In a nutshell, it has tremendous benefits! Many of the traditional organic sunscreen filters, such as avobenzone, break down readily following sun exposure. It is estimated that 30% to 90% of the applied avobenzone degrades after one hour of sun exposure, requiring frequent sunscreen reapplication.
 Not BEMT. This new filter is more photostable and can provide prolonged photoprotection. This means it could be combined with other filters to increase stability, delivering higher Sun Protection Factor (SPF) photoprotection in-between sunscreen applications.
 Another concern has been systemic absorption of sunscreens. Many organic sunscreen filters have been found in urine, including avobenzone, oxybenzone, octisalate, octocrylene, and octinoxate. In contrast, BEMT remains primarily on the skin surface with minimal penetration and negligible systemic absorption. This provides for improved safety due to its high molecular weight of 627.8 g/mol. Sunscreen filters with smaller molecular weights, such as oxybenzone (228.2 g/mol) and avobenzone
 (310.4 g/mol), are more readily absorbed.
 Some sunscreen filters, such as oxybenzone and octinoxate, have been implicated as endocrine disruptors due to their estrogen-like effects. These same two filters demonstrate coral reef concerns as they produce reef bleaching. BEMT did not show any hormonal effects in androgen or estrogen receptor competitive binding assays. It also did not demonstrate any toxicity in testing or photoallergy or phototoxicity in human testing.
 Cosmetic elegance is also important in sunscreen formulations. BEMT is oil soluble and can be placed in the oil phase of traditional sunscreen oil-in-water emulsions. This provides for smoother application and increased skin softness. It can be used in sunscreens, lip balms, moisturizers, and facial cosmetics. Further, BEMT is invisible when applied to darker Fitzpatrick skin types, unlike zinc oxide and titanium dioxide, which leave a white cast. BEMT is also hypoallergenic and can be used in sensitive skin formulations and in individuals with diseases characterized by barrier disruption, such as eczema, atopic dermatitis, and psoriasis.
 Since BEMT is in the oil phase of the sunscreen, it can be more resistant to removal by water contact or sweating. This is why BEMT is the most common sunscreen filter in Europe and Japan.
 The hope is that the US FDA approval of BEMT will tremendously advance photoprotection science, allowing sunscreen manufacturers to build more effective, safer sunscreens with improved aesthetics for all skin types.
 KEY TAKEAWAYS
 Protects against both UVA and UVB rays
 Low skin absorption
 Photostable
 Cosmetically elegant
